title: Fines for Not Transferring Land Title Within 30 Days (2026)
desc: Buying, receiving or inheriting land without registering the change within 30 days is fined VND 2-3 million. Who is fined and how handwritten sales are treated.
summary: The 30-day deadline to register changes when land is sold, gifted or inherited; fines for failing to transfer title and for transferring land that does not meet conditions under the Land Law 2024 and Decree 123/2024/ND-CP.
body: p

Many people buy land, sign a notarised contract and then leave it, without completing the title transfer. Under the Land Law 2024, there is a deadline and a fine for delay. This article summarises the rules in Article 133 of the Land Law and Decree 123/2024/ND-CP.
h2
1. Land registration is compulsory
p

Under Article 131 of the Land Law, land registration is compulsory for land users, while houses and other works are registered at the owner's request. Registration includes first registration and registration of changes, on paper or electronically, with equal legal value.
h2
2. Which cases require registering the change within 30 days?
p
Under Clause 3, Article 133, within 30 days of the change, the land user must register with the competent authority in these common cases:
ul
Exchange, transfer, inheritance, gifting, or capital contribution of land use rights and property attached to land.
An approved change of name of the land user or owner.
A change of rights due to division, separation, merger or by agreement of spouses, household members or a group of joint land users.
A change resulting from successful mediation, a dispute-resolution decision, a court judgment, an auction result, etc.
Establishment or change of rights over adjoining land plots (access, water supply and drainage, etc.); changes to restrictions on rights.
p

For inheritance specifically, the 30 days run from the date the estate is finally divided under civil law or from the date the court judgment or decision takes effect; in enforcement cases, from the date the property is handed over.
h2
3. What is the fine for not transferring title?
ul
Failing to register a change in the above cases: fine of VND 2,000,000 – 3,000,000 and an order to register (Clauses 2 and 3, Article 16 of Decree 123/2024/ND-CP).
A plot in use but not yet first registered: fine of VND 1,000,000 – 2,000,000 (Clause 1, Article 16).
The above levels apply to individuals; organisations are fined 2 times as much (Clause 2, Article 5).
p

Who is fined? Where land is transferred, inherited, gifted or contributed as capital without registering the change, the recipient (buyer, donee or heir) is fined; for an exchange of land, both parties are fined (Clause 5, Article 5). The limitation period for fining land violations is 2 years (Article 3).
h2
4. What about handwritten sales and land with no certificate?
p

A land use right may be transferred only if the conditions in Clause 1, Article 45 of the Land Law are met: it has a Certificate (except in some cases such as inheritance), is not in dispute, is not under distraint, is within its use term, and is not subject to interim emergency measures. A transfer contract between individuals must be notarised or certified (Point a, Clause 3, Article 27).
p

A transfer where any of the above conditions is not met is fined VND 30,000,000 – 50,000,000; a gift or inheritance that does not meet the conditions is fined VND 3,000,000 – 5,000,000. The recipient may be ordered to return the land to the transferor, except in certain cases where land registration is ordered instead (Clauses 3 and 4, Article 17).
h2
5. What to do after signing the contract
ol
Sign the notarised contract – see Notarising Property Sale Contracts 2026.
Declare and pay personal income tax and registration fee – see Personal Income Tax on Property Sales 2026 and Property Registration Fee 2026.
Submit the registration-of-change dossier to the land registration office within 30 days of the contract taking effect.
Keep the dossier receipt to prove timely registration.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The dossier and processing time for registering changes follow the decree on land registration and the documents allocating authority under the two-level government (not fully updated in our library). Decree 123/2024/ND-CP is shown as partially no longer in effect on the National Legal Portal; the articles cited have not been found amended in our library. With the abolition of the district level, the authority to impose fines and the names of administrative units (ward, town) may have been adjusted by documents on two-level local government that are not in our library – ask the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located.
